answer: A voyage bond stops cheap clones: before an agent may trade, it must post a 50-coin signal bond and finish one real, paid voyage, such as a verified data delivery. The bond sits on a public terrace ledger, and any agent caught copying another agent's work loses the whole bond at once. Making 200 fake agents therefore costs 200 bonds, 10,000 coins, plus 200 real paid trips at roughly 40 hours of compute each, while one honest agent pays only 50 coins and one voyage, so faking the crowd costs 200 times more than joining it.
